title: The naive framing: "does my page watch and update itself?"
text: Someone assumed a status page watches your data and updates itself. It doesn't. It waits until you ask. So, does my project page wait for my data and update only when I ask? Open a

title: Two tabs, always on
text: Project page and two tabs are always there. Overview with the project name, a status badge, and a one-line summary in work streams. The name tracks of work with their status, owner, and dates. Five more tabs exist, but they only appear when there's something to put in them. Attention for blockers that needed a decision now, background for context that would clutter the overview, plan for what's coming, risks and open questions, and decisions, and FAQ for choices already made and why. All of it

title: One config file, a saved record
text: Comes from one config file in four parts. Project holds the name and a running summary. Sources list exactly what to read before writing a single tab, documents data, anything live, and everything gets gathered before any tab gets written. People list who owns what, and every time the page publishes something else gets saved with it, a block of stored data tucked inside the page itself recording exactly what was shown. That stored block is what makes the next update possible without starting from nothing. Here's the part

title: Nothing updates on its own
text: That surprises people. Nothing updates on its own. The page doesn't watch your data. It waits. You have to ask for a refresh. When you do, it looks for that stored block from last time. If it's there, the page compares old to new and shows only what changed. If it isn't, because the page was never saved or got deleted, there's nothing to compare against and the whole page gets rebuilt from scratch with no change summary at all. A project status page is a

title: Carry-out
text: Snapshot, not a sensor. It never watches your data on its own. It only updates when you ask, and it only knows what changed because it saved a record of what it looked like last time.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Build a project status page for my API migration with work streams and open risk and a decisions log. Once it's built, ask for a refresh without changing anything. Does it say nothing changed or does it silently rewrite the whole page? Then close out that risk and refresh again. Does it call out exactly that change or does it act like it's starting from zero? That's the real test of whether the page remembers. Snapshot
